item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Getting Started
item.description: In this series of articles, I will share my experience of building a GPU SaaS platform from scratch.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Shared Proxy and SSH Access
item.description: Part 10: add a shared storage proxy, switch the accessor to dufs, and expose GPUUnit SSH through sidecars and frp.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Security and Metrics
item.description: Part 11: harden runtime workloads with capability drops, shared-memory sizing, egress isolation, and expose runtime and Nvidia GPU metrics.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - OverlayBD Cold Start
item.description: Part 12: explain how OverlayBD converts OCI images into a lazy-pullable block format and why that changes cold start for large GPU images.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Queue-First Ingress
item.description: Part 13: record the runtime-side serverless contract on GPU units and enqueue invocations durably through NATS JetStream before any worker executes them.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Activator Dispatch
item.description: Part 14: add a dedicated activator that consumes ingress invocations, selects or creates GPUUnit workers, and publishes worker-targeted dispatch messages.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Worker Sidecar
item.description: Part 15: add a serverless worker sidecar, define a UDS framework contract, and return results and metrics through NATS.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Worker Lifecycle
item.description: Part 16: add activator-owned worker lifecycle management, prewarm pools, idle scale-down, and metrics-driven worker state.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Invocation Result Store
item.description: Part 17: add a ScyllaDB-backed result-store consumer for durable serverless invocation metadata and control-plane result lookup.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Runtime Control Plane Split
item.description: Part 18: split the runtime into a reconciler-only controller manager and a separate runtime API server.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - DRA Package Allocation
item.description: Part 19: replace runtime-side GPU counting with DRA-backed package allocation, ResourceClaim status, and controlled runtime packages.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - The requirement spec
item.description: How to write a requirement document for a GPU SaaS platform, and what should be included in the document.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - GPU Virtualization with HAMi
item.description: Part 20: add HAMi virtual GPU packages on top of the DRA allocation contract.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Reliable Serverless Execution
item.description: Part 21: add queue retry policy, dead-letter handling, execution state classification, and runtime behavior changes for serverless GPU execution.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Runtime Ops Boundaries
item.description: Part 22: harden runtime with Secret/TLS config, split RBAC, probes, metrics, and deployment boundaries while keeping audit in the control plane.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - The design spec
item.description: Let's write down the design spec for our GPU SaaS platform.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Runtime Bootstrap in Go
item.description: Part 4: build the first runnable single-cluster runtime baseline with production-oriented engineering habits.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Operator Baseline
item.description: Part 5: move the project onto a standard kubebuilder layout, switch the API to Echo, and let requests create real custom resources.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Useful Operator Contracts
item.description: Part 6: add operation idempotency, Swagger docs, clearer controller failure status, and the first runtime template.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - One Unit, One Controller
item.description: Part 7: collapse stock and runtime into one GPUUnit resource, seed stock explicitly, and hand off warm units into active runtime.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Storage Lifecycle
item.description: Part 8: introduce GPUStorage, mount persistent data into GPUUnit, and separate data lifecycle from runtime lifecycle.

item.title: Building a GPU SaaS Platform - Storage Data Jobs
item.description: Part 9: add storage prepare jobs, the first accessor path, and recovery state to GPUStorage.
